subject: koala
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: koala gripping a eucalyptus branch stand.
Style: pixel art.
reasoning:
I'm sketching the design for a pixel-art koala clinging to a eucalyptus branch stand, with a base, vertical trunk, and leaves, aiming for a compact but visually rich composition using the pixel kit's tile and cell painting tools.

For the face I'll use pixel-art decal planes for eyes and nose on the head, with a big black oval nose box, while the head itself uses a tiled fur texture. I'm setting up grey fur ramps with cream belly tones, pale pink-tufted ears, bark browns, and leaf greens, then using cellPaint with noise-based dithering to shade the body and define the cream belly patch by facing direction.

Now I'm building the skeleton: hips as the root joint, a spine chain curving up through chest height, then a head joint parented to the spine tip with a jaw joint attached. I'm blocking out the torso as a pear-shaped set of boxes, with a wider hip box sized to sit naturally on top of the branch geometry.

Then I'm shaping the head as a large box with a dark nose box at the front, and round ear cylinders placed symmetrically with pink inner and cream outer layers for a soft, rounded look.

Switching to stepped boxes for pixelated round ears, then placing small plane-based pixel art eyes and a shiny-textured nose box on the front face of the head.

Now I'm figuring out the jaw and muzzle geometry — a lower box for the mouth positioned beneath the head with a joint for aiming, giving it a pale pink-gray muzzle tone and a whitish chin tuft.

For arms, I'm working out limb placement from shoulder joints down to the hands, having the koala grip a forward branch or small twig fork extending off the main branch so it looks like it's holding on naturally.

Actually, a vertical trunk might work better—having the koala seated at a branch junction hugging a thin trunk directly in front of its chest feels like the classic koala pose.

That trunk placement would put it right in front of the face, which is bad. Let me shift the trunk off to the side instead, placing it at the koala's right so one arm hugs the trunk while the other grips a perch branch in front — asymmetric but more natural-looking.

I'll simplify: a vertical trunk behind the koala going up with leaves, and a perch branch extending forward along Z that the koala straddles like sitting on a horizontal limb, legs on either side, hands gripping the branch near the hips.

I'm positioning the feet and hands to clasp around the branch sides so the koala hugs it naturally, then placing the trunk behind at an angle with a vertical perch branch, and sketching out a stepped plinth base with a grass/dirt top layer for the scene's foundation.

I'll scatter leaf cards along the trunk using pixelated textures, then add small finger nubs and pale claws to the hands. For bark, I'm using a cellular paint approach with brown tones and vertical grain streaks to give the trunk texture, and a tiled box pattern for the base.

Writing leg and chain code...

Continuing the arm chain, I calculate elbow bend direction outward with appropriate hint vectors, then define hands and finger boxes attached at the wrist. Now I'm building the spine chain parented to hips with joint points rising from the pelvis up through the torso, naming each segment accordingly.

For the body shapes, I'm placing blocky boxes for the torso and hips with explicit bone assignments, adding a small cream-colored belly patch that protrudes slightly from the torso front. Then I position the head joint and head box, checking its front depth and vertical extent before starting on cheek details.

I'm now adding fluffy cheek boxes flanking the head, then shaping a darker nose box with a tiny highlight for shine. For the eyes, I'm placing pixel-art planes at the head's front plane, sketching a rounded 5x5 pattern, and moving on to think about ears next.

For the ears, I'm layering outer gray fur boxes with an inner cream fluffy rim pushed slightly forward for a plush look, then starting to set up a jaw joint attached to the head.

Still placing jaw geometry...

Now I'm planning the leaf cards using a pixel-art leaf texture, generating curved twig paths from the trunk and sampling frames along each sweep to place leaf cards with randomized size, lean, bend, and flow so they look naturally scattered across the branches.

I'm adding grass tufts at the base and deciding to skip glow effects, keeping all props rigidly attached to the hips joint since that's the required root bone. For the floor layout, I'm stacking a plinth box and grass layer so the trunk starts right above them at the correct height.

Now I'm working out the perch height and post dimensions so the koala sits properly above the floor, then sweeping the trunk as a tapered polyline shape and building the perch as a rod using the available sweep/rod helper functions.

I'm keeping sides at 6 for a low-poly look and staying within the color budget since paints don't count against it. For bark texture I'm writing a simple cell-paint function that mixes random variation with periodic banding, then moving on to defining the leaf twigs.

I'm placing four twigs branching from the trunk's upper region, varying their start and end points to create a natural asymmetric spread, plus one lower twig near the koala's side. I'm also confirming the random helper works as a plain function for tile positioning, and setting up imports from the builder SDK and pixel kit before writing the actual construction code.

For the feet, I'm adding small box claws at each toe position offset from the foot tip, plus a slightly larger box for the foot pad itself, attaching everything to the last joint in the leg chain the same way I'll handle hands. I'm assigning dark skin tones to the hands and lighter claw colors to the fingers, then adding a fluffy pad detail to the feet before finalizing the limb coloring sweep.
